questions.question_text:
A prism has a semicircular cross-section of diameter $12$ cm and is $9$ cm long.
Find its volume in exact form, in terms of $\pi$.

options.why: Used the diameter $12$ as the radius, giving $\tfrac12\pi(12^2)$ instead of $\tfrac12\pi(6^2)$.
Used a full circle $\pi r^{2}$ for the cross-section instead of a half circle $\tfrac12\pi r^{2}$.
Stopped at the cross-sectional area and did not multiply by the $9$ cm length.

questions.solution_text:
The cross-section is a semicircle of radius $r = 6$ cm.
$A = \frac{1}{2} \times \pi \times 6^{2}$
$= 18\pi\text{ cm}^{2}$
$V = Ah$
$= 18\pi \times 9$
$= 162\pi\text{ cm}^{3}$

questions.question_text:
A quarter-round moulding is a prism with a quadrant cross-section of radius $8$ cm, and it is $6$ cm long.
Find its volume, correct to $1$ decimal place.

options.why: Used a semicircle $\tfrac12\pi r^{2}$ instead of a quadrant $\tfrac14\pi r^{2}$ for the cross-section.
Used a full circle $\pi r^{2}$ instead of a quarter circle for the cross-section.
Stopped at the cross-sectional area and did not multiply by the $6$ cm length.

questions.question_text:
A prism has a sector cross-section of radius $10$ cm and angle $72^{\circ}$, and it is $3$ cm long.
Find its volume in exact form, in terms of $\pi$.

options.why: Used a full circle $\pi r^{2}$, ignoring the $\tfrac{72}{360}$ fraction of the sector.
Left out the length, giving the sector area $20\pi$ as the volume.
Doubled the angle fraction, effectively using $144^{\circ}$ instead of $72^{\circ}$.

questions.question_text:
A prism has a sector cross-section of radius $5$ m and angle $120^{\circ}$, and it is $9$ m long.
Find its volume, correct to $1$ decimal place.

options.why: Used a full circle $\pi r^{2}$, ignoring the $\tfrac{120}{360}$ fraction of the sector.
Stopped at the cross-sectional area and did not multiply by the $9$ m length.
Used a $60^{\circ}$ fraction instead of $120^{\circ}$, halving the sector area.

questions.question_text:
A half-round trough has a semicircular cross-section of diameter $14$ cm and is $20$ cm long.
Find its volume, correct to $1$ decimal place.

options.why: Used a full circle $\pi r^{2}$ for the cross-section instead of a semicircle.
Used the diameter $14$ as the radius instead of halving it to $7$.
Stopped at the cross-sectional area and did not multiply by the $20$ cm length.

questions.solution_text:
The cross-section is a semicircle of radius $r = 7$ cm.
$A = \frac{1}{2} \times \pi \times 7^{2}$
$= \frac{49}{2}\pi\text{ cm}^{2}$
$V = Ah$
$= \frac{49}{2}\pi \times 20$
$= 490\pi$
$= 1539.3804\ldots$
$\approx 1539.4\text{ cm}^{3}$

questions.question_text:
A prism has a semicircular cross-section of radius $5$ cm and is $16$ cm long.
Find its volume, in $\text{cm}^{3}$, correct to $1$ decimal place.

options.why: Used a full circle for the cross-section, calculating $\pi \times 5^{2} \times 16$.
Used a quadrant for the cross-section, calculating $\tfrac14 \times \pi \times 5^{2} \times 16$.
Forgot to square the radius, calculating $\tfrac12 \times \pi \times 5 \times 16$.

questions.question_text:
A prism has a semicircular cross-section of radius $4$ m and is $10$ m long.
Find its volume, in $\text{m}^{3}$, correct to $1$ decimal place.

options.why: Used a full circle for the cross-section, calculating $\pi \times 4^{2} \times 10$.
Used a quadrant for the cross-section, calculating $\tfrac14 \times \pi \times 4^{2} \times 10$.
Left out the length, giving $\tfrac12 \times \pi \times 4^{2}$ as the volume.

questions.question_text:
A pipe is a $12$ m long prism whose inside is a semicircle of radius $2$ m and whose outside is a semicircle of radius $3$ m (a semicircular shell).
Find the volume of the shell material, in m³, correct to $1$ decimal place.

options.why: Used the outer semicircle alone without subtracting the inner semicircle.
Used full circles instead of semicircles for the ends, giving $\pi(3^2-2^2)\times12$.
Subtracted the radii before squaring, using $\tfrac{1}{2}\pi(3-2)^2\times12$ instead of $\tfrac{1}{2}\pi(3^2-2^2)\times12$.

questions.solution_text:
The shell cross-section is the outer semicircle minus the inner semicircle.
$A = \frac{1}{2}\pi (3^{2} - 2^{2})$
$= \frac{5}{2}\pi\text{ m}^{2}$
$V = Ah$
$= \frac{5}{2}\pi \times 12$
$= 30\pi$
$= 94.2477\ldots$
$\approx 94.2\text{ m}^{3}$

questions.question_text:
A prism has a sector cross-section of radius $9$ cm and angle $40^{\circ}$, and it is $8$ cm long.
Find its volume, in $\text{cm}^{3}$, correct to $1$ decimal place.

options.why: Used a full circle for the cross-section, calculating $\pi \times 9^{2} \times 8$.
Left out the length, giving $\tfrac{40}{360} \times \pi \times 9^{2}$ as the volume.
Doubled the angle fraction, calculating $\tfrac{80}{360} \times \pi \times 9^{2} \times 8$.
